latin: Ex diuina bonitate potest sumi ratio praedestinationis aliquorum et reprobationis aliorum, et sola diuina uoluntas est ratio quod istos reprobet et illos eligat in gloriam.
translation: From divine goodness the reason for the predestination of some and the reprobation of others can be drawn, and the divine will alone is the reason he reprobates these and elects those to glory.
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch2, from Latin at farmer1998:11324

sources.text: Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae, 1, q. 23, a. 5
sources.pico_relation: Edelheit identifies this article as the source of Pico's thesis on predestination and reprobation

doctrine: The thesis holds that the reason for predestining some and reprobating others is drawn from divine goodness, while the divine will alone accounts for who is reprobated and who elected (farmer1998:11324). Edelheit reports that Pico states that the reason of the predestination of some and the reprobation of others can be inferred from divine goodness, and that only the divine will is the reason for condemning the latter and electing the former to glory, locating the thesis in Thomas's Summa theologiae, 1, q. 23, a. 5 (edelheit2022:10367). Farmer groups this thesis with 2.2-9 under the divine omnipotence/free will problem (farmer1998:11348).
historiography: Edelheit (2022) quotes Pico's Latin at page 220 of the 900 Theses alongside the opening of Thomas's response in the Summa, 1, q. 23, a. 5 (edelheit2022:10390).

quotations.text: In thesis 6 Pico states that the reason of the predestination of some and the reprobation of others can be inferred from divine goodness, and only the divine will is the reason for condemning the latter and electing the first to glory.

not_established: Not established by the sources consulted.
